claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires a third-party Ubisoft Connect account and launcher to play online.

citations.review_text: the game itself is fun, it's literally UNO it's kinda hard to mess that up. However, the entire experience is made miserable by being forced to use the barely functional Ubisoft Connect launcher. I just wanna play UNO with my friends, I don't want to deal with an unnecessary convoluted piece of software

🎭 The Experience It’s UNO. You know how to play it. Your friends know how to play it. You sit down thinking it’s going to be a casual 10-minute card game, and 45 minutes later, relationships are ruined, screaming matches have occurred over a stacked +4, and someone has deleted Discord. Core gameplay is solid, nostalgic, and genuinely a blast when it actually functions.  The Good Classic Rules & Customization: You can toggle popular house rules (7-0 hand swaps, Stacking +2/+4s, Jump-In), which makes matches way more chaotic and fun.  Fun DLC Themes: DLC packs like UNO Flip!, Ray man, and Show 'Em No Mercy actually add interesting mechanics to spice things up.  Great with Mates: If you can get a lobby full of friends, it’s peak banter. The Bad (Why the Steam Recent Reviews are "Mixed")Ubisoft Connect Bloat: You buy a basic $10 card game on Steam, only to be forced to launch Ubisoft Connect on top of it. Account linking errors, launcher crashes, and random login bugs plague the startup process.  Connection / Net code Issues: Joining lobbies or staying connected in online matches can feel like a toss-up. Random disconnections, lobby freezes, and host migrations ruin matches mid-game.  DLC Nickel-and-Diming: The base game feels bare-bones, and Ubisoft aggressively pushes cosmetic board themes and rule expansions as extra paid DLC.  Rage-Quitting / Bot Takeover: When playing with randoms online, the moment someone gets hit with a +4, they quit. They get replaced by an AI bot that either plays like a grandmaster or completely throws the match.  💡 The Verdict "A top-tier party game trapped inside a bottom-tier launcher."  If you can catch it on sale for $3 - $4, and you have a dedicated group of 3 or 4 friends to play custom lobbies with, it's worth picking up for a quick laugh. Otherwise, if you just want to play card/board games on PC without the Ubisoft headache, grab Tabletop Simulator instead.

[b]Introduction :[/b]
UNO est l'adaptation officielle du célèbre jeu de cartes, développée et éditée par Ubisoft, sortie en décembre 2016. Le principe est celui que tout le monde connaît depuis les repas de famille : se débarrasser de ses cartes en premier, balancer des +4 au pire moment et crier UNO. Sur le papier, impossible de rater ça. Et pourtant.

[b]Ce que j'ai aimé :[/b]
[list]
[*]🃏 Les règles du UNO sont fidèlement reproduites, avec les règles maison activables (empilement de +2/+4, échange de mains) qui font le sel des vraies parties
[*]🎨 L'interface est propre et lisible, les parties s'enchaînent vite — le cœur du jeu de cartes fonctionne
[*]🛋️ En local entre amis sur le même écran, ça reste un bon moment sans prise de tête
[/list]

[b]Ce que j'ai moins aimé :[/b]
[list]
[*]📡 Le online est une loterie : déconnexions à répétition même avec une connexion parfaite, parties qui gèlent, hébergement qui exige parfois de bidouiller sa box — pour un jeu dont l'intérêt principal EST le multijoueur, c'est rédhibitoire
[*]🔌 Ubisoft Connect obligatoire par-dessus Steam, avec son lot de lancements qui échouent et de comptes à lier — une friction inutile pour un simple jeu de cartes
[*]💸 La politique de DLC est gonflée : des thèmes de cartes vendus à l'unité sur un jeu déjà payant, alors que le contenu de base est squelettique
[*]👋 Les rage quits ne sont quasiment pas sanctionnés, donc la moitié des parties en ligne se terminent par un abandon dès que quelqu'un perd
[*]🤝 L'intégration des amis Steam est bancale : invitations peu intuitives, et des fonctions annoncées comme le vrai couch co-op via Remote Play qui fonctionnent mal
[/list]

[b]Conclusion :[/b]
UNO version Ubisoft, c'est un bon jeu de cartes enfermé dans une mauvaise application. Le online instable ruine l'expérience, Ubisoft Connect n'a rien à faire là, et les DLC cosmétiques sur un contenu aussi maigre passent mal. Prenez un vrai paquet de cartes à 3 €, ou jouez-y uniquement en local si vous l'avez déjà.…

Don't buy it. Ubisoft, much like EA, force you to download and register with their launcher in order to play their games even if you buy them on Steam.

This means, even if you bought it on Steam or were given it by a friend on Steam, that you will not be able to play it if Ubisoft's platform bugs out and removes it from your Ubisoft Plus library or Ubisoft themselves just removes it from your library for whatever reason.

This is what they have done to me and Ubisoft's customer service is terrible; anytime I open a support ticket to deal with the issue, they don't give me time to get around to responding and instead just close the ticket to force me to put in another ticket.

This has been going on for well over a couple of years now and I've just given up because there's no point in trying to get help from Ubisoft.

So, I cannot play the game my friend got for me with him anymore, because Ubisoft's platform is terribly made and Ubisoft themselves are a terrible company with terrible customer service.

Even though, again, it was given to me on STEAM. My friend bought it for me ON STEAM. NOT on UBISOFT PLUS.

Steam shouldn't be letting companies force you to install other platforms just to buy the games you buy on Steam, especially since it can lead to situations like mine.

Funny how Disclaimer in loading screen says to not play if under influence.. Like.. I'm playing uno not flying a plane how hard can it be???

Horrible software, where I'm lucky to get a game working within the first half hour, and requires a third party login that simply doesn't work for me half the time, then locks me out of my own account. I keep giving it a few more years, after all Ubisoft is a very small company, and if anything it just gets worse.

cohorts.summary: Longer term players run into game-breaking loops, freezing turns, launcher login gates, and unexpected language bugs.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe game-breaking bugs where players become trapped in infinite loops of drawing cards or having turns skipped indefinitely.

citations.review_text:
Ubisoft are taking stupid pills with this one.   

I get into a match... someone puts down a +4 on my ass, but then the game decides no one is allowed to have a turn after I pickup 4 cards, and skips them all, 

When it was my turn again, I had to pickup another 4 cards, then it skipped everyone's turn and repeated this over and over. 

Nobody could play their cards, the only thing they could do was sit and watch it go through the motion of skipping their turns and have my deck get bigger and bigger from one singular +4 that had been put there about 30 turns ago. 


This repeated over and over until the game crashed.


Ubisoft have contracted an outsider dev team to run Uno. New dev team means there will be teething issues... especially since they decided to change the backend, the frontend, you name the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ end, so of course this is expected. Have you looked at what they've done to the UI?


 ...So I waited a few months for the bugs to get fixed.
  

Uno launched in a completely different language than English and just when I was about to look for the settings button, the game crashed. Good job.

[h1] Funniest matches of UNO I played [/h1]
The first five matches of uno flip were fine with occasional bugged cards. Then in the sixth match my friend could not stop drawing even though he pulled mutiple playable cards. After 60 cards the game settled down and allowed him to play one card. Then the next player also had to draw, even though she had playable cards in her deck. When she reached 37 cards, the draw pile disappeared and we were trapped in an infinite circle of Skip Everyone. After 3 minutes of helplessly watching all of our cards light up without being able to do anything, we sadly had to quit the match.

We then tried to play regular uno and here is when the bugs (Or is this straight up failure?) became very apparant: The custom decks and animation we equipped, did not work at all, except for one player. Selecting a color or whose deck you wanna switch with, was only possible with the arrow keys for two players. The music was getting louder or quieter randomly. Those obnoxious saxophones will haunt me in my dreams and purgatory probably sounds like that too. One player could call out uno anytime, regardless of how many cards there were in the deck. 

All in all, I never laughed that hard in my life. 10/10 recommend for people who like buggy games.
(0/10 for my friends I played with, but those reviews you can read for themselves)

claims.claim: Reviewers report unexpected language changes, such as the game launching in Polish instead of English.

citations.review_text: When I tried playing uno, Ubisoft started updating then wanted me to log in. Since it has been almost a year since I played it I put in multiple gmails and passwords that I would use. Until after 3 attempts it stated that "Your Account has been suspended" ALL BECAUSE I DIDNT KNOW MY GMAIL AND PASSWORD. I later closed the game then re opened it. I finally got into uno without needing to log in until I noticed that the language was set to polish even though I live in New York. I went into settings changing it then I was finally, FINALLY ready to play UNO. I joined a game, and not even 10 seconds into the game. I SOMEHOW GOT KICKED BECAUSE OF MY NETWORK, EVEN THOUGH I USE ETHERNET. This game and Ubisoft itself has become horrible, and I want Ubisoft to FIX THERE GAMES.

Besides 3rd Party launchers being the bane of my existence, the language somehow automatically switched to Polish on launch, so I had to guess where the language settings were. This happened twice btw and now the game auto-switches me to Polish every time I boot the game up for some reason. I'm not Polish nor live anywhere near Poland

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game experiences crashes, freezing, and loading delays during matches.

citations.review_text:
Super unstable while playing.
loading that takes forever
timing out
game getting stuck making people quit mid game
terrible job done ubisoft

We litterally can't play a single full game with my friends, because of either one or multiple of the following reasons:

- Lobbies often time out
- Game crashes
- Either friends or I can't get into one's lobby
- First card drafted is glitchy. Best case scenario: try every color until you get it right. Worst case scenario: no card can't be played (not even a joker or a +4) and players are condemned to draft until death.
- Successful challenges on +4 will both get the attacker and the defender 4 additional cards...

It is outrageous that a game, which has been out for almost a decade and patched over and over again only to get paid DLCs or cosmetics, won't see any of its critical and game breaking issues resolved despite the numerous complaints from the community.

In short: a buggy cashgrab joke.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires the third-party Ubisoft launcher or account login to play.

citations.review_text:
Game is fine because it doesn't contain the customer service and upper management of Ubisoft.
Ubisoft stole my account claiming I had to prove I was the owner. I gave them receipts and a timeline of my purchases and reward redemptions. They claim it is insufficient proof and that they cannot prove I own the account.  

A massive Merry Kirkin, and many Luigi's to you Ubisoft

Great game when it works.

Unless you have a lot of patience with Ubisoft and their janky launcher, this might be a good game for you.

The Ubisoft game launcher came out in 2009 and seemed to work well.
They rebranded in 2012 to Uplay. Around 2018 the launcher became buggy and largely unstable.
In 2020 Ubisoft rebranded again to Ubisoft Connect and all of the bugs and instability came with it.

The core problem is reliability. The launcher needs a full reengineering of its initialization and state management. The reoccurring hangs, spool corruption, and fragile background processes show the underlying code is brittle and poorly handled.

I've had 4 brand-new higher end gaming PC's during this time, so they cannot blame hardware on these issues.

Ubisoft should reengineer their embarrassing launcher, or Mattel should revoke their digital licensing rights for UNO and let a different publisher or developer take over their beloved game.

Almost a decade of frustration. Enough is enough...

When I tried playing uno, Ubisoft started updating then wanted me to log in. Since it has been almost a year since I played it I put in multiple gmails and passwords that I would use. Until after 3 attempts it stated that "Your Account has been suspended" ALL BECAUSE I DIDNT KNOW MY GMAIL AND PASSWORD. I later closed the game then re opened it. I finally got into uno without needing to log in until I noticed that the language was set to polish even though I live in New York. I went into settings changing it then I was finally, FINALLY ready to play UNO. I joined a game, and not even 10 seconds into the game. I SOMEHOW GOT KICKED BECAUSE OF MY NETWORK, EVEN THOUGH I USE ETHERNET. This game and Ubisoft itself has become horrible, and I want Ubisoft to FIX THERE GAMES.

This is the first game that made me wish there was a star rating system. Originally I would give Uno a 4.5/5 but as of recently that would go down to a 3-3.5/5. My only original complaint was Ubisoft being really not my favorite to work with and needing to create a whole account can be a hassle. Overall the game worked beautifully and my friend group played consistently. However, they recently redid their whole UI and it completely destroyed what we loved. It additionally removed the ability to upload your own pfp which sucks - please correct me if there's a way to do that still. The UI change made my whole gaming group stop playing Uno with hesitance to return. Even before the UI change there were still a lot of bugs and it wasn't uncommon for a player to be randomly dropped from the game. It is wonderful to have the ability to play Uno online as its one of the best party/card games. I just hope they made QOL improvements to make the game just that bit more enjoyable to all players.

Its honestly impressive how a simple card game can be messed up so badly, because you have to have the Ubisoft launcher after purchase. And it is pretty much just malware on your computer. The game will randomly kick a person just because, some nights it wont, some nights its just unplayable. I wouldn't say to waste your money on this, you can probably just find a uno-like game on a web browser
